summary: The crew eats a gray, gooey single-celled-protein breakfast in the mess hall, trading jokes about how the machines can't replicate real food. Mouse brags that he wrote the Agent training program and offers Neo a secret encounter with "the woman in the red dress" he designed, pitching indulgence as human nature while the others mock him. Morpheus enters, orders everyone to twelve-hour standby, and announces he is taking Neo to see the Oracle, then leaves. Neo, not knowing who "her" is, is told by Tank that it is the Oracle.

what_changes.before: Neo does not know who Morpheus means when he says he is taking him to see "her."
what_changes.after: Neo learns the person is the Oracle, the figure he is being taken to meet.
what_changes.evidence: NEO: See who? TANK: The Oracle.

what_changes.before: Neo is a newcomer eating with the crew, absorbing their casual banter about the food and the world.
what_changes.after: Morpheus singles him out for a special, privileged step: "I'm taking Neo to see her," marking him as the one being taken to the Oracle.
what_changes.evidence: MORPHEUS: I want everyone on twelve-hour standby.  We're going in.  I'm taking Neo to see her.

what_changes.before: Mouse joins the general breakfast conversation about the food.
what_changes.after: He elevates himself by revealing authorship of the training program and offering Neo a private, sensual encounter, casting himself as an enabler against the "hypocrites."
what_changes.evidence: MOUSE: So I understand you've run through the Agent training program?  You know, I wrote that program.

event_hint.one_line: The crew shares a last casual meal before Morpheus announces they are going in to see the Oracle, singling Neo out for the journey.

objects_that_matter: the woman in the red dress
uncertain: Whether this meal is breakfast specifically or just called that; the script says "breakfast" but time of day is unspecified.
What "going in" precisely entails beyond reaching the Oracle.

minds.wants: To impress the crew and especially Neo by claiming authorship of the Agent training program and offering him a private encounter with 'the woman in the red dress,' thereby converting his technical authorship into social and sexual currency.
minds.feels: A hungry, adolescent pride in his own cleverness; he has built something forbidden and wants witnesses to it. The pitch about 'denying our impulses' is less a philosophy he has reasoned toward than an excuse to make his own appetite respectable.
minds.shows: Braggadocio and a leering, conspiratorial ease — 'sidles up,' casts himself as a worldly enabler, dismisses the others as hypocrites. He performs casual control over something taboo.
minds.basis: He announces 'I wrote that program,' then pivots immediately to offering Neo 'a more personalized milieu' with a woman he 'designed,' and frames refusal as self-denial. The crew's 'Here it comes' and 'digital pimp' tell us this is a rehearsed routine.

believes_about.belief: That Neo will be grateful and impressed by the offer, and that this is the natural way to bond with the newcomer.
believes_about.wrong_because: Neo has no stake in Mouse's ego and no interest in the construct; he only asks 'Of who?' The offer lands as noise, not a gift.

believes_about.belief: That the others mock him out of prudishness or jealousy — that they are 'hypocrites' who secretly want what he offers.
believes_about.wrong_because: Their contempt ('Shut up, Mouse,' 'The digital pimp hard at work') is boredom and mild disgust, not repressed desire; they have seen this performance before and find it tiresome.

minds.wants: To keep the meal easy and to puncture Mouse before Mouse can work up a full head of steam — to police the table's mood.
minds.feels: Wearied familiarity with Mouse's routines; he has heard the Cream of Wheat and red-dress pitches enough to predict them and to pre-empt them with a groan.
minds.shows: Terse, timed put-downs — 'Shut up, Mouse' the instant Mouse gets going, and 'Here it comes' as Mouse sidles to Neo. He lets the others do the color commentary.
minds.basis: He cuts Mouse off twice at the exact moments Mouse is about to escalate, and signals the crew with 'Here it comes,' showing he knows the script by heart.

believes_about.belief: That Mouse is a predictable nuisance whose provocations are more embarrassing than dangerous.
believes_about.wrong_because: This is only the crew's casual reading; it has no access to whether Mouse's neediness is harmless. (Nothing here proves it either way.)

minds.wants: To deflate Mouse's self-importance with wit rather than brute force — to win the exchange on style.
minds.feels: Amused contempt, and a sharpness that enjoys landing a line. Switch treats Mouse as material, not a threat.
minds.shows: Dry, clever jabs — correcting Mouse's logic ('technically neither did you') and branding him 'The digital pimp hard at work.' Cool, unhurried superiority.
minds.basis: The two lines are precisely aimed — one undercuts Mouse's premise, the other names his role — and both are delivered as sport, not anger.

believes_about.belief: That Mouse is a figure of fun whose grandstanding is safely contained by mockery.
believes_about.wrong_because: Like the others, Switch reads Mouse as harmless clown; the scene gives no reason to think Mouse is anything but that, but the mockery is a settled verdict, not a tested one.

minds.wants: To look after Neo — to make the newcomer feel fed, included, and initiated — while staying easy with the rest of the crew.
minds.feels: A warm, big-brother protectiveness. He is the one who physically serves Neo ('Here you go, buddy') and the one who closes the scene by supplying the name Neo lacks.
minds.shows: Buddy-casual warmth and a steady, explanatory helpfulness. He plays along with the banter but keeps Neo in his care.
minds.basis: He slides Neo the food with 'buddy,' sits with the crew, and, when Morpheus names 'her,' Tank is the one who answers Neo's 'See who?' with 'The Oracle.'

believes_about.belief: That Neo is a green newcomer to be gently shepherded through the crew and the world.
believes_about.wrong_because: Tank cannot yet know Neo is being set apart as 'the One' Morpheus will stake the crew on; his warmth is toward a rookie, not a prophecy.

minds.wants: To anchor the banter in fact — to be the one who names what they are actually eating and why — keeping the mood light but grounded.
minds.feels: A practical, slightly proud competence; he makes the fuel that keeps them alive and is content to be the straight man explaining it.
minds.shows: A calm, factual interjection about the single-celled protein, delivered without rancor. He doesn't join the mockery of Mouse; he just supplies the real answer.
minds.basis: His speech is the only technical description in the scene, delivered plainly amid the jokes, and the facts match the ship's self-sufficiency (he also 'makes' the alcohol in sc-073).

believes_about.belief: That Neo is simply another mouth to feed and brief, a new crewmate to be oriented.
believes_about.wrong_because: Dozer has no reason yet to see Neo as anything but a newcomer; the special errand Morpheus is about to announce is not his to know.

minds.wants: To take the crew's measure, to belong enough to eat with them, and to learn what he can without exposing how far behind he is.
minds.feels: A wary, absorbing curiosity; he is still new enough that everything — the food, the jokes, the hierarchies — is data. He is quietly out of his depth.
minds.shows: Sparse, reactive participation — he scoops the food, asks 'Of who?' and 'See who?' — letting the crew perform while he watches.
minds.basis: He says almost nothing of his own initiative; his only lines are questions that reveal gaps ('Of who?', 'See who?'), and he accepts Tank's serving and Tank's answer.

believes_about.belief: That Mouse is simply an eager, slightly strange crewmate offering information.
believes_about.wrong_because: Neo has no framework yet for Mouse's neediness or for how the crew reads him; he takes the offer at face value rather than as a status play.

believes_about.belief: That Morpheus is an unknowable, imposing figure whose plans happen around Neo rather than to him.
believes_about.wrong_because: This scene reassigns Neo from bystander to the specific object of Morpheus's errand ('I'm taking Neo to see her'), but Neo still doesn't grasp the weight Morpheus places on him.

minds.wants: To move the crew to readiness and to take Neo the next, decisive step — to the Oracle — without explanation or debate.
minds.feels: A taut, forward-leaning certainty. He carries the whole weight of the prophecy (and, unknown to the crew, the fresh warning from Cypher in sc-073) and refuses to let it show as doubt.
minds.shows: Command and economy — he enters, issues one order, names the mission and the one exception ('I'm taking Neo to see her'), and leaves without lingering. He does not explain 'her' to Neo; the gap itself is instruction.
minds.basis: His entire presence is four lines that reorganize the room: standby, 'We're going in,' and singling Neo out. He doesn't answer Neo's 'See who?' — Tank does — which keeps Morpheus's authority intact and the destination mythic.

believes_about.belief: That Neo is ready, or ready enough, to be taken to the Oracle and to begin carrying the prophecy.
believes_about.wrong_because: Neo still doesn't even know who 'her' is and is processing the crew's casual world; Morpheus's certainty runs well ahead of Neo's actual readiness — the same certainty Cypher warned is fatal in sc-073.

believes_about.belief: That Cypher, left on the ship, remains a loyal crewman while Morpheus takes the risk of going in.
believes_about.wrong_because: Cypher has already bargained to hand Morpheus to the Agents (sc-074); Morpheus's 'going in' is walking straight into the trap Morpheus does not know exists.

connects_back: sc-073: Cypher's warning that Morpheus has believed in five previous 'Ones,' all dead — the certainty with which Morpheus now takes Neo to the Oracle is exactly the faith Cypher called a 'mindjob.'
sc-074: Cypher's deal to deliver Morpheus to Agent Smith — the 'going in' Morpheus announces is the movement Cypher has already sold, though no one at this table knows it.
The crew's casual, lived-in banter about the Matrix's fake food establishes the normalcy that Cypher has rejected and that this meal momentarily restores before the mission.
sets_up: ev-021 (The Oracle's Prophecy): Morpheus taking Neo to 'see her' and the crew going on standby is the departure that leads directly to the Oracle's apartment and her test of Neo.

ev-022 (Mouse's Death and the Hotel Raid): Mouse's introduction here — his authorship of programs, his presence on the crew — establishes the character who will be left behind and killed at the Hotel Lafayette.
ev-023 (Escape and Extraction): The 'going in' and Cypher's unobserved presence on the ship set the conditions for Cypher to kill Dozer and shoot Tank during the extraction.
Neo's singling-out ('I'm taking Neo to see her') deepens the divide Cypher resents, which fuels Cypher's later actions.
dramatic_function: This scene restores the crew's ordinary humanity — appetite, humor, hierarchy — as a last calm before the mission, while quietly doing two things at once: it marks Neo as chosen (raising him in the crew's eyes and in the story's), and it stages the departure under a false premise, since the audience knows Cypher has already sold that departure. The banter and Mouse's indulgence-vs-duty pitch also give the film its thesis about what 'being human' costs, right before the crew is asked to pay it.
